scope: All 24 selected terrain patches in four-date imagery/DSM/WorldCover panels; full panels additionally inspected for the three retained prospects and Kalibangan context. Post-outcome exploratory visual interpretation.
retention_semantics: Screening leads are places with an unresolved compact raised feature worth record concordance and non-invasive reconnaissance. Retention supplies no age, archaeological probability or novelty claim.

decisions.alternative: compact dune remnant or a previously recorded mound
decisions.observation: An irregular, relatively dark compact patch persists across all four dates, with a distinct positive DSM support separated from nearby elongated dune crests. Its 9.09 ha support and +6.92 m peak-minus-ring descriptor justify a concordance check. It lies within the unresolved Ganweriwala mapping buffer, so it cannot be called an independent or new site.
decisions.next_test: Resolve Ganweriwala's surveyed mound plan and the unpublished-to-this-study Cholistan candidate coordinates first; if the feature remains unidentified, obtain permitted surface observations and a ground elevation profile.

decisions.observation: The small positive support lies on the same directional dune texture as the surrounding landscape. Four-date imagery supplies no distinct occupation surface or independent contrast.
The support is embedded in continuous dune texture and repeats the morphology of nearby raised sandy areas. Compactness alone does not separate it.
The positive support follows an elongated crest aligned with the surrounding dune field, without a separate surface form.
A small raised fragment follows the surrounding directional sandy relief. It does not have the distinct dark compact surface seen at B01-T0115.
The support follows an irregular curved crest that expands substantially at the lower terrain threshold. The surrounding repeated dune form explains the geometry.

decisions.alternative: tree canopy beside a transport embankment
decisions.observation: The support overlaps a persistent dark grove beside a major straight transport corridor. WorldCover assigns approximately 62% of its support to trees; the DSM can include canopy height.
A dark vegetated patch lies beside modern built ground. Approximately 63% tree and 9% built cover provide direct rival explanations for its surface elevation.
The patch is embedded at a modern settlement margin and overlaps substantial tree cover. Its high surface elevation cannot be isolated from those objects.
The patch follows a rectilinear cultivated parcel with trees. Approximately 65% crop and 26% tree cover, together with the imagery, explain the DSM high without a distinct mound form.
A small persistent dark grove occupies the support. WorldCover's approximately 87% tree assignment and the imagery support a canopy explanation.

decisions.alternative: tree canopy in the Harappa vicinity
decisions.observation: The small support is largely tree covered and falls within the conservative Harappa reference-point buffer. It is retained as local context, without an independent-site interpretation.
decisions.next_test: Use the published Harappa site plan to locate this patch relative to recorded mounds; separate ground surface from canopy before archaeological interpretation.

decisions.observation: The approximately +49.79 m peak-minus-ring high is part of a prominent natural hill among the region's repeated rough relief. The threshold support is not a settlement outline.
The raised support coincides with irregular rough high ground among cultivation and similar nearby hills. No separate archaeological morphology is resolved.
A small support sits within continuous rough relief beside a larger ridge. The four-date imagery supplies no independent compact occupation surface.
The support is a small rough knoll among multiple larger natural highs and drainage corridors. Its positive height alone provides insufficient discrimination.
An elongated, irregular support follows a natural high with nearby cultivation and repeated relief. Its 24.57 ha threshold area does not define an archaeological site.
The support follows an L-shaped rough ridge among irregular fields. Its curved ridge form and repeated local geology explain the extracted high.

The distinct compact raised bare support coincides with the published Kalibangan archaeological reference at map scale. It is a known-site context check, not a new candidate. The 11.70 ha support is a threshold subset, not the site's published extent.
decisions.next_test: Compare the extracted support with a georeferenced excavation/site plan; use it to assess method limitations rather than as a discovery.

decisions.observation: The high overlaps a rectangular dark vegetated parcel. Tree canopy and modern parcel form provide direct rival explanations.
The large support overlaps continuous dark vegetation. WorldCover assigns approximately 82% of the support, and 99.7% of the inner window, to trees.

decisions.strength: low; modern and natural alternatives unresolved
decisions.alternative: small natural remnant, modern disturbed ground or an already recorded mound
decisions.observation: A small bare or sparsely covered patch persists within the crop-field grid and coincides with a compact positive DSM support. The 1.53 ha threshold support and +6.42 m peak-minus-ring descriptor remain unexplained at available resolution. Support expands to 9.36 ha at the lower threshold, so the extracted boundary is unstable.
decisions.next_test: Check the complete local site gazetteer and historical land use; inspect higher-resolution permitted imagery or the ground to distinguish a mound from farm structures, earthmoving and a natural remnant before any dating claim.

decisions.observation: A small high lies within a rectilinear parcel and near modern built ground. The available imagery supplies no separate raised archaeological morphology, and modern disturbance remains a direct explanation.

decisions.strength: low; cultivation and historical canopy unresolved
decisions.alternative: natural raised remnant, cultivated mound, old canopy or modern ground alteration
decisions.observation: A compact positive support overlaps an irregular parcel within the cultivated grid; part of the patch differs from neighboring winter-green plots and remains discernible in the October image. The 6.03 ha support and +5.93 m peak-minus-ring descriptor justify a ground-surface check. WorldCover assigns about 85% of the support to crop; farming does not establish or exclude archaeological origin.
decisions.next_test: Check local records and earlier land cover, then acquire a ground elevation profile and permitted surface observations. Determine whether the DSM high comes from ground relief, historical trees or modern alteration before interpreting occupation.
